subject: AuthN snapshots & bridge-letter coordination for SOC 2 Type II
messages:
From: markus_klein@redwood.com
To: alice@auditas.com, security@medisure.com
Cc: laura_bennett@redwood.com
Date: Fri, 20 Nov 2026 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: AuthN snapshots & bridge-letter coordination for SOC 2 Type II

Hi Alice / MediSure security team,

As we discussed in the kickoff, MediSure will need a short set of supporting artifacts ahead of the SOC 2 Type II bridge review next month. To make this as targeted as possible, please confirm you can accept the following scoped extracts from Redwood: 

- MFA enrollment export (per-user enrollments, second-factor types, enablement dates) for the audit window.
- Authentication log slices: successful/failed auth events for a chosen 30-day window within the audit period (we can provide several 30-day samples).
- Access review evidence: a snapshot of the last quarterly privileged-access review (names, review result, reviewer).
- Retention mapping doc that ties our auth/retention settings back to SOC 2 control IDs (we've attached a control map).
- A signed bridge-letter draft confirming no material control changes outside of the documented exceptions.

Attached is an initial control mapping and a proposed bridge-letter template (draft) so you can flag gaps. We'd like to deliver the log slice securely (preference: S3 upload with one-time link); let us know SFTP if you need it.

Please confirm acceptance of the scope and any preferred formats or redaction requirements. If there's an exact 30-day window you want (e.g., high-traffic month), we can prioritize that slice.

Thanks,
Markus Klein
Senior Sales Engineer | Redwood Inference
markus_klein@redwood.com
Redwood Inference
Attachments: control-mapping-2026Q3.xlsx, bridge-letter-draft-Redwood.pdf
From: alice@auditas.com
To: markus_klein@redwood.com, laura_bennett@redwood.com
Cc: security@medisure.com
Date: Mon, 23 Nov 2026 07:34:00 -0800
Subject: Re: AuthN snapshots & bridge-letter coordination for SOC 2 Type II

Markus — thanks for the clear list. A couple quick clarifications before we confirm: 

1) Audit window: please provide one primary 30-day auth-log slice plus an alternate 30-day slice from the same reporting year. Preferential windows: Aug 1–Aug 31, 2026 and Nov 1–Nov 30, 2026. If only one is possible, prioritize Aug.

2) Formats: auth logs can be zipped JSON/CSV. MFA enrollment export as CSV is fine. Access review snapshot can be Excel or PDF.

3) Redaction: we require user identifiers to be consistent across artifacts (pseudo IDs okay) and a short mapping file that shows how pseudonyms map to real IDs in a separate, encrypted artifact if needed. Please confirm whether Redwood can produce a pseudonym map for the slices or whether MediSure will accept redacted identifiers.

4) Bridge letter: we'll want a signed PDF with a minor attestation clause about no control changes after the end of the monitoring period. If you can provide a draft by COB Nov 22 we can review and return a signed copy by Nov 24.

5) Delivery: S3 pre-signed URLs are preferred; DocuSign for the bridge if you want us to countersign.

Can you also nominate a technical contact who can answer follow-up questions about log fields (e.g., event_type, outcome, ip_address, device_id, mfa_used)?

Best,
Alice Gomez
Senior Assurance Manager | Auditas Assurance
alice@auditas.com

From: neha_kapoor@redwood.com

Date: Mon, 23 Nov 2026 11:05:00 -0800
Subject: Re: AuthN snapshots & bridge-letter coordination for SOC 2 Type II

Hi Alice / MediSure team — thanks for the checklist. Quick answers and delivery plan below.

1) Windows: we can provide the primary Aug 1–Aug 31, 2026 slice and an alternate Nov 1–Nov 30, 2026 slice.

2) Formats & filenames (we will upload to S3 with pre-signed URLs):
   - mfa-enrollment-export-20261101.csv (columns: user_id, enrollment_date, method, last_used)
   - auth-log-slice-20260801-20260831.zip (zipped JSON lines; fields: timestamp, user_id, event_type, outcome, ip_address, device_id, mfa_used)
   - auth-log-slice-20261101-20261130.zip (alternate slice)
   - privileged-access-review-2026Q3.pdf (signed reviewer attestation page included)
   - retention-mapping-2026Q3.xlsx (control id mapping)

3) Redaction approach: we will pseudonymize user_id for the audit slices and provide a separately encrypted pseudonym_map.key file to your security contact if you need linkage back to real IDs. If MediSure prefers full identifiers, we can produce a redacted-vs-real mapping under an encrypted channel — let us know.

4) Bridge letter: attached is a revised draft (bridge-letter-draft-Redwood.pdf) with the attestation clause updated per your note. We can provide a signed PDF by EOD Nov 23.

5) Technical contact: cc'd is Laura Bennett (laura_bennett@redwood.com), our Head of Security Operations, who can field any schema questions or provide sample rows.

Deliverables ETA: S3 links for the primary slice and MFA export by Nov 24 17:00 PT; signed bridge letter by Nov 23 18:00 PT.

If that timeline works, I'll proceed with the upload and send the one-time links via encrypted email.

Thanks,
Neha Kapoor
Security Compliance Manager | Redwood Inference
neha_kapoor@redwood.com
Attachments: mfa-enrollment-export-20261101.csv, auth-log-slice-20260801-20260831.zip, bridge-letter-draft-Redwood.pdf, control-mapping-2026Q3.xlsx

Neha / Laura — this plan works. Thank you for the filenames and the pseudonym approach; that aligns with MediSure's data handling constraints. Two small follow-ups before we close scope: 

- Please include a short README with each upload describing field definitions and any inferred fields (e.g., how device_id is generated).
- Can you provide a one-paragraph keystore/rotation note for the review (how keys are rotated, last rotation date, and KMS used)? We don't need keys, just the operational note to tie to key-management control references.

If you can attach the README and rotation note with the S3 upload, we'll run a quick sanity check and provide the signed bridge letter back to you by Nov 24 morning PT.

We'll expect: S3 links + encrypted pseudonym_map.key + README.txt + keystore_rotation_note.pdf. Once received, Auditas will validate the slices and get back within 48 hours.

Thanks — Alice
